# Catalogue

Every accepted diagram, by the relationship it shows. Before you draw, write your own one sentence ("the viewer sees [one change], which explains [one relationship]"), then find the one or two entries below whose **shows** is nearest to it, whatever their subject. Open their sheets (every moment, in order) with your image reader, and take what **borrow** names. A familiar subject is not a match: a cache diagram may be nearest to a queue's picture.

Do not start from the same picture every time. If your sentence is about time, proportion or a part of a whole, the nearest entry is not a row of boxes.

## Flow: something travels

### access-then-tunnel

**Shows:** A remote user is checked against an identity provider first, and only an allowed request continues through the link to the private app.  
**Picture:** Vertical stack of user, gate card, link label, private boundary with connector and app; an identity provider card off to the right of the gate. (6 moments)  
**Fits:** auth before proxying, a policy check before routing, a bouncer in front of a backend  
**Not for:** When the check happens after or in parallel with the request; the order is the claim.  
**Borrow:** The side trip: the gate's wire goes right to the provider, and the answer comes back violet ('allowed' written in the gate card) before the main column continues. The last moment lights the user again to close the round trip. 6 moments.  
**Avoid:** Shares the vertical-stack look with tunnel-traffic; do not use both in one piece. A copy that skips the violet return hides that the check answers before anything moves.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/access-then-tunnel.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### git-add-commit-push

**Shows:** A change moves one step at a time from the working area to a staging area, into local history, and then out to a shared copy.  
**Picture:** Vertical chain of four cards with command labels on the wires; the first three inside a dashed 'your machine' boundary, the last outside. (5 moments)  
**Fits:** a deploy pipeline, a draft to review to publish flow, promotion between environments  
**Not for:** When steps can be skipped or reordered; the single chain says each one is required.  
**Borrow:** Each card's sub-line carries the state ('hello.txt modified' to 'clean', '0 commits' to '1 commit, ahead 1'); the boundary shows which steps stay local. One moment per step plus a start. 5 moments.  
**Avoid:** Do not light the whole chain at once; one card per moment is the rhythm.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/git-add-commit-push.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### api-build-what-happens

**Shows:** A spec is prepared twice at build time, and a request at run time reads just one prepared page.  
**Picture:** Horizontal pipeline of five boxes on top, two branches dropping down, a dashed run-time box at the bottom right. One of three pipeline pictures with api-build-why-await and api-build-plan. (9 moments)  
**Fits:** build vs run time, compile then serve, precompute then look up  
**Not for:** When work really happens per request; the split says it does not.  
**Borrow:** A dashed box marks the run-time part so the reader sees which work is skipped later; each box's sub-line changes to say what it did ('one file per page', 'cache hit · 0 entries'). 9 moments.  
**Avoid:** The three api-build figures share one pipeline look; reuse one, not all three. Long pipelines at this size shrink text to unreadable.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/api-build-what-happens.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/forge.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### api-build-why-await

**Shows:** A setup step cannot finish until an earlier stage has worked out every value it needs.  
**Picture:** Horizontal pipeline of five boxes, the last two inside a dashed config box. One of three pipeline pictures with api-build-what-happens and api-build-plan. (7 moments)  
**Fits:** a blocking dependency, an await on startup, config that needs data from a slow step  
**Not for:** When stages can run in parallel; the single row says they cannot.  
**Borrow:** Show the blocked state first (the last box says 'cannot derive them'), then run the upstream boxes, then the release ('config loaded'). Problem before resolution. 7 moments.  
**Avoid:** Near-identical picture to api-build-plan; if you need both the problem and the fix, keep one layout and change only sub-lines.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/api-build-why-await.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/forge.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### api-build-plan

**Shows:** A cached step reads its result on a hit and only processes the source on a miss, so later steps get everything they need from it.  
**Picture:** Horizontal pipeline of five boxes with one drop-down branch labelled 'on a miss'. One of three pipeline pictures with api-build-what-happens and api-build-why-await. (7 moments)  
**Fits:** a cache with a fallback, memoisation, a lookup that sometimes fetches  
**Not for:** When there is no fallback path; the branch would be decoration.  
**Borrow:** Run the miss path first (branch lit, violet return up the branch), then the hit path with the branch faded out. One side branch carries the alternative. 7 moments.  
**Avoid:** Same picture as api-build-why-await; do not show both. A copy that draws hit and miss at once loses the contrast.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/api-build-plan.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/forge.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### nt-tank-b

**Shows:** A backlog grows when work arrives faster than it leaves, fills, refuses, then drains.  
**Picture:** Three equal panels in a row (ARRIVALS, BACKLOG, WORKERS) with wires on the notches. Template: rates. (5 moments)  
**Fits:** queues, buffers, rate limiters, connection pools  
**Not for:** When the subject is how the level changes over time; use a plot (curve template).  
**Borrow:** Rates as panel text; refuse the in-wire and turn the backlog red when full. 5 moments.  
**Avoid:** Do not add per-item cards; panels must share a height so wires sit on notches.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/nt-tank-b.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/notched.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### r21a3

**Shows:** A resolver asks root, then .com, then the site's server once, keeps the answer, and the next lookup stops at its cache.  
**Picture:** Browser card, resolver panel whose detail line narrates, three servers in a column on elbow wires through one junction; the second lookup fades the servers. Template: ask. (10 moments)  
**Fits:** DNS, recursive lookups, a cache in front of several backends  
**Not for:** When the subject is the naming hierarchy itself.  
**Borrow:** The panel's detail line carries the narration; fade the servers for the cached pass.  
**Avoid:** More than three servers; captions repeating the panel line.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r21a3.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r21a3.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### r25g

**Shows:** A pipeline stops at the first failure: build passes, tests fail, deploy never runs.  
**Picture:** A push card then build, tests and staging panels in a row on wires; build turns green, tests red, staging fades. Template: handoff. (5 moments)  
**Fits:** CI/CD, gated stages, any chain that halts on a failure  
**Not for:** When stages run at once; use spans.  
**Borrow:** Green for passed, red for the failure, faint for what never ran; end on the faint stage. 5 moments.  
**Avoid:** Running the wire into the stage that never ran.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r25g.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r25g.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### r26n

**Shows:** A coordinator asks three databases to prepare; all yes means commit, one no means all roll back. Both outcomes shown in turn.  
**Picture:** Coordinator and three database panels along the top with lines down; prepares fan out as rows, yeses come back as rows; the second round has a red NO and three roll backs. Template: turns. (9 moments)  
**Fits:** two-phase commit, votes, quorum, all-or-nothing writes  
**Not for:** When only one outcome matters.  
**Borrow:** Rows go out to all, answers come back one by one; the coordinator's detail counts them ('2 of 3 yes'); a no is red.  
**Avoid:** Showing only one outcome when the subject names two.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r26n.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r26n.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### r26p

**Shows:** A sign-in stores a session and sends back a cookie with its id; the next request carries the cookie, the server looks the id up and knows who is asking.  
**Picture:** Browser, server and session store along the top with lines down; seven messages as rows, the cookie's real value in their words. Template: turns. (7 moments)  
**Fits:** cookies, session tokens, any id handed out and shown again  
**Not for:** When the token carries its own data (a signed token); nothing is looked up.  
**Borrow:** The id in every row that carries it (Set-Cookie: sid=41f, look up 41f); end on the answer to the browser.  
**Avoid:** Answers drawn from the asker: each row starts at its sender.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r26p.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r26p.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### lanes-handover

**Shows:** Work passes between three workers over the same 100 ms: the main thread asks the network and sits idle until the answer comes, then hands drawing to the GPU, so the page shows only when the last hand-over is done.  
**Picture:** Three notched lanes stacked (MAIN THREAD, NETWORK, GPU), a tick row in each filling with time, upright wires between lanes at each hand-over instant ('GET /data', '200', 'draw'), a dashed 'Page visible' line over them all. (4 moments)  
**Fits:** a page load, a request fanning through services, a job queue handing to workers, any wait whose cause is another worker  
**Not for:** When only one worker is busy, or when durations are the whole story and nothing hands over; use spans or periods.  
**Borrow:** Time runs across, workers stack down; every gap in one row is explained by a wire to the row that is busy then; tick rows fill to the same instant in every lane each moment. 4 moments, one per hand-over. For hatched lanes (no frames), the Lanes pattern: lane() + activity() + handover().  
**Avoid:** Wires at instants that do not line up with a row's start or stop; more than three lanes; a moment line that sits under the frames (draw it as a guide after them).  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/lanes-handover.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/picked.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

## Phase: one thing moves through states

### do-lifecycle

**Shows:** One object goes from cold to active to hibernating and back to cold, keeping its storage while its memory comes and goes.  
**Picture:** One state card (header with status word, rows ID / MEMORY / STORAGE) under a request box. Same picture as container-lifecycle. (5 moments)  
**Fits:** a cache with an expiry, a lease, a session timeout, a process that sleeps and wakes  
**Not for:** When many instances matter at once; one card hides how many exist.  
**Borrow:** The status word in the card header carries the state (COLD, ACTIVE, HIBERNATING); a memory bar fills blue, greys, then empties, while the storage square stays put to show what survives. 5 moments.  
**Avoid:** Near-duplicate of container-lifecycle; pick whichever has the rows you need. Do not add arrows between states; the card changing in place is the point.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/do-lifecycle.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### container-lifecycle

**Shows:** A workload does not exist until a request arrives, starts, runs, idles, and is torn down to nothing.  
**Picture:** One state card under a request box; empty grey placeholder panels with a sentence stand in for 'nothing exists'. Same picture as do-lifecycle. (6 moments)  
**Fits:** scale to zero, a serverless function, a pod's life, a lease  
**Not for:** When the thing is always on; the empty placeholders would be false.  
**Borrow:** Grey dashed placeholder with a plain sentence ('Awaiting request', 'No running instance') for the absent states, so the start and end are visible. Status word plus CPU bar for the live states. 6 moments.  
**Avoid:** Near-duplicate of do-lifecycle; do not draw both for one idea. Placeholder text must be one short line, not an explanation.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/container-lifecycle.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### r25f

**Shows:** Servers are upgraded one at a time, each taken out and put back, so the service never stops answering.  
**Picture:** One segments strip of four equal servers, the one being upgraded picked and named OUT, then v2; a caption under it narrates. Template: bands. (9 moments)  
**Fits:** rolling deploys, draining nodes, one-at-a-time maintenance  
**Not for:** When traffic moving between servers is the story; use wires.  
**Borrow:** Each part's words are 'version  name'; two moments per server (out, then back on v2); end with all on v2. 9 moments.  
**Avoid:** Changing the parts' sizes: the shares stay equal.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r25f.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r25f.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### r27b

**Shows:** A cached response is fresh for 60 s, served stale for 30 s more while a fresh copy is fetched, then gone, so the next request waits for the origin.  
**Picture:** One segments strip of three periods, each as wide as it lasts ('0 to 60 s / fresh', '60 to 90 s / stale', 'after 90 s / gone'); a light slides along; the caption says what a request gets at that point. Template: periods. (6 moments)  
**Fits:** cache lifetimes, stale-while-revalidate, leases, tokens that expire, grace periods  
**Not for:** When several things' times are compared; use spans.  
**Borrow:** Periods sized by how long they last; the light stops just before a boundary ('59 s: still fresh') to make the edge felt.  
**Avoid:** The dots-on-a-line timeline.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r27b.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r27b.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

## Comparison: two side by side

### container-connectivity

**Shows:** A workload's local disk is gone when it stops, while the stores reached through bindings keep their data.  
**Picture:** Vertical column: client, front box, instance card with a LOCAL DISK bar, then a stacked persistent-storage list; a side wire runs from the front box down to the list. (11 moments)  
**Fits:** ephemeral vs durable storage, scratch space vs a database, cache vs source of truth  
**Not for:** When both stores live as long; the contrast is the whole point.  
**Borrow:** End on the stopped state: the instance goes grey and its disk bar empties while the store rows keep their blue marks. The side wire shows the front box, not the workload, holds the bindings. 11 moments.  
**Avoid:** Text is tiny at this density; a copy with more than four store rows becomes unreadable. Do not make the side wire look like a data path from the instance.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/container-connectivity.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### nt-spans-b

**Shows:** The same three calls end to end in a row, then stacked when started together.  
**Picture:** Three single-part segments bars, end to end, then moved to x 0 and stacked. Template: stack. (4 moments)  
**Fits:** serial vs parallel work, sequential vs batched writes  
**Not for:** When there is no total worth comparing.  
**Borrow:** Light each bar in turn, then one at beat moves all into a stack with a new caption. 4 moments.  
**Avoid:** Keep the caption clear of the stack (below the last row).  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/nt-spans-b.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/notched.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### r27d

**Shows:** The same values kept by row and by column: summing one column reads every value one way and only that column's the other.  
**Picture:** Two segments strips of the same twelve real values (ids, names, quantities, prices), one in row order, one in column order, each part named under it; a light sweeps what is read. Template: layouts. (5 moments)  
**Fits:** row vs column stores, data locality, struct of arrays, grouping for reads  
**Not for:** When the sizes of the parts are the story; use bands.  
**Borrow:** Real values in the parts, their kind under them; one sweep covers all, the other only what is needed; the caption counts the reads.  
**Avoid:** Drawing both arrangements the same, or a single bar standing for a column.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/r27d.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/trial/r27d.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

## Decomposition: a whole taken apart

### bt-budget

**Shows:** A fixed amount of time is split into parts, and one part takes half of it.  
**Picture:** Proportional segments under a 1-second rule; each segment lit in turn with a bracket below. Same segmented-bar picture as bt-url. Use this, not a timeline, for where time goes. (7 moments)  
**Fits:** a latency breakdown, a memory budget, where money or time goes  
**Not for:** When parts overlap or run in parallel; the bar says they add up in order.  
**Borrow:** Widths are proportional to the value; the overall rule above states the total. Walk each segment, then return to the largest one as the closing moment ('500 ms, half of it'). 7 moments.  
**Avoid:** Same bar as bt-url, but here widths are data; do not make widths arbitrary.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/bt-budget.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/built.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### bt-url

**Shows:** A single string is made of parts, and each part is read by a different party for a different job.  
**Picture:** One segmented bar with labels below and a bracketed caption under the lit segment. Same segmented-bar picture as bt-budget. (6 moments)  
**Fits:** an address, a file path, a version string, a record's fields  
**Not for:** When the order of parts does not matter or parts nest.  
**Borrow:** Under each lit part a bracket with a 2-3 word role ('who to ask', 'what to fetch'); the last moment revisits the part that matters most ('picks the handler'). 6 moments.  
**Avoid:** Widths are not data here; do not imply they are.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/bt-url.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/built.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### nt-ring-c

**Shows:** Keys hash onto a circle cut open into a strip; each server owns the stretch before it, and a new server takes only the front of one stretch.  
**Picture:** One proportional segments bar 0 to 360 degrees, one part per server plus a wrap-around part; a zero-width part grows out of a neighbour. Template: strip. (4 moments)  
**Fits:** consistent hashing, shard ranges, partition ownership, IP ranges  
**Not for:** When ownership is not a contiguous range; the strip claims order.  
**Borrow:** The joiner exists from the start at width 0 and grows via a cut beat, so nothing else moves; light the one stretch affected. 4 moments.  
**Avoid:** Do not draw the circle or a key travelling; do not add a user or client card.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/nt-ring-c.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/notched.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### nt-line-b

**Shows:** Requests counted by how long they took: most are fast, a long thin tail is slow.  
**Picture:** One plot as bars, revealed left to right, the tail red. Template: curve. (3 moments)  
**Fits:** latency distributions, file sizes, any histogram  
**Not for:** When the viewer needs exact percentiles; use nt-line-c.  
**Borrow:** Reveal the distribution in three steps, ending on the tail. 3 moments.  
**Avoid:** Do not label every bar.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/nt-line-b.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/notched.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

### nt-line-c

**Shows:** A spread split into bands by share: a wide band of fast ones, a thin sliver at the end.  
**Picture:** One proportional segments bar, one part per percentile band, lit in turn, the last red. Template: bands. (4 moments)  
**Fits:** percentiles, where time or money goes, a budget split  
**Not for:** When parts overlap.  
**Borrow:** Part names carry share and bound ('50%  ≤120 ms'); end on the band users notice. 4 moments.  
**Avoid:** Widths must be data.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/nt-line-c.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/notched.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

## Containment: inside and outside

### tunnel-outbound

**Shows:** A connector inside a private network opens connections outward to a public edge, so nothing inbound has to be allowed.  
**Picture:** Dashed boundary box holding one connector, an edge box above it, two parallel vertical wires with square sockets. (3 moments)  
**Fits:** a reverse connection, an agent dialling home, a long-lived outbound link through a firewall  
**Not for:** For short request lines; the sockets say 'held open', so a one-shot call drawn this way lies.  
**Borrow:** Direction by order of lighting: the inside box lights first, then the wires, then the outside box. Square sockets on both ends of a persistent link. Only 3 moments.  
**Avoid:** Do not add a request travelling over the wires; this figure is about the link existing, not traffic.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/tunnel-outbound.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### tunnel-traffic

**Shows:** A link is built first, then a route is added on the public side, and only then can a user's request reach the private service.  
**Picture:** Vertical stack: user, public boundary box, link box, private boundary box with connector and service. A route chip appears inside the public box. (5 moments)  
**Fits:** setting up DNS before traffic flows, registering a route, mounting a service behind a gateway  
**Not for:** When setup order does not matter; the build-up implies a required sequence.  
**Borrow:** Build the picture across moments (the link appears in moment 2, the route chip in 3) so the setup steps are the story; a small caption 'enable tunnel' at the top in moment 1.  
**Avoid:** The marks are small and grey; a naive copy ends up with a figure where nothing reads as lit. Shares the vertical-stack look with access-then-tunnel.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/tunnel-traffic.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### container-isolation

**Shows:** A request hits a front process, which then boots a separate sandbox that holds the workload.  
**Picture:** Plain request label, a front box, and a VM card wrapping a container chip, stacked top to bottom. (4 moments)  
**Fits:** a sandbox inside a VM, a plugin running in its own process, a job inside a pod  
**Not for:** When the wrapper is shared by many workloads; one-to-one nesting says each gets its own.  
**Borrow:** The nested card appears only when the request reaches it (moment 3), so creation-on-demand is shown by absence first. 4 moments.  
**Avoid:** Very small; a copy with more than three levels loses the nesting. Its first half overlaps container-request-path.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/container-isolation.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### nt-tree-b

**Shows:** A name is found from the root down: each level only knows who runs the next one inside it.  
**Picture:** Nested zones (root around .com around shop.com) with a chip for the answer; a still picture. Template: frames. (1 moments)  
**Fits:** DNS, file paths, scopes, org units, nested permissions  
**Not for:** When levels are peers, or the subject is the order of steps rather than the nesting.  
**Borrow:** Nesting carries the hierarchy, so no wires; one moment, no animation.  
**Avoid:** Do not add a resolver card with wires beside the frames; do not animate it.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/nt-tree-b.png` · **Source:** `src/canvas/notched.ts` (short form: copy and change it)

## Hierarchy: levels

### tunnel-identity

**Shows:** One logical link is served by more than one connector, and either can carry it.  
**Picture:** One named box on top, a junction dot, two branch wires down into a dashed boundary with two connectors; one branch lit at a time. (2 moments)  
**Fits:** one name backed by several replicas, a load-balanced pool, a failover pair  
**Not for:** When the members do different jobs; the identical boxes say they are interchangeable.  
**Borrow:** Two moments only: light branch A, then branch B, with the other branch greyed. The junction dot makes the one-to-many split explicit.  
**Avoid:** Two moments are enough; adding traffic or a failure turns it into leader-election.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/tunnel-identity.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### container-request-path

**Shows:** A front process routes each request to its own stateful object, which in turn starts its own sandbox.  
**Picture:** Tree: request and front box on top, two object cards (each with ROUTE/HOOKS/SLEEP chips), a VM card under each. (10 moments)  
**Fits:** requests keyed to per-user actors, sharded workers, one session object per client  
**Not for:** When routing is random; the fixed A/B branches say a key decides.  
**Borrow:** Run branch A fully (route, object, sandbox) then branch B, then rest everything grey in the last moment. Sub-chips on a card show its operations without extra boxes. 10 moments.  
**Avoid:** Sub-chips are tiny; do not put more than three. Running both branches doubles the length; cut to one branch if the second adds nothing.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/container-request-path.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

## Network: many to many

### workers

**Shows:** Each location asks a central controller once, and from then on a copy of the code runs right next to that location.  
**Picture:** Fan-in: three location chips in a top row, one controller at the bottom; a worker card with a cell grid appears under each location in turn. Same layout as container-placement. (12 moments)  
**Fits:** edge caching, code deployed per region, lazy replicas, on-demand workers spun up near users  
**Not for:** When placement is fixed in advance or there is only one site; the slow build-up then reads as a cost that does not exist.  
**Borrow:** Three beats per location (ask controller, controller places the card, card answers the location), repeated so the pattern is learned; the final pass shows a location using its existing card with no trip to the controller. 12 moments.  
**Avoid:** Near-duplicate of container-placement (same row-plus-hub picture). Pick one; do not copy the full 12 moments if the repeat teaches nothing new; three locations is the most this layout holds.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/workers.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### container-placement

**Shows:** Each location's first request goes to a scheduler, which places an instance there; later the network has one per location.  
**Picture:** Fan-in: three location cards with 'send request' rows on top, a scheduler at the bottom, container cards appearing under each location. Same layout as workers. (10 moments)  
**Fits:** autoscaling across regions, a placement service, lazy replicas  
**Not for:** When placement is static or global; the per-location build-up implies on-demand.  
**Borrow:** Each location's own row lights as the request leaves it; the final moment shows all three instances placed and idle as a summary. 10 moments.  
**Avoid:** Near-duplicate of workers: same row-plus-hub layout and same three-beat repeat. Choose one; never stack both in one piece.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/container-placement.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### leader-election

**Shows:** When the leader's heartbeats stop, a follower asks for votes and becomes the new leader.  
**Picture:** Horizontal row of three node cards inside a dashed cluster box, labelled wires (heartbeat, request vote) between them, a looping heartbeat wire underneath. (4 moments)  
**Fits:** failover, lock handover, primary/replica promotion  
**Not for:** For more than three nodes or real voting counts; it shows the handover, not the protocol.  
**Borrow:** The dead node fades to pale blue rather than vanishing; the role word in each card (leader, follower, candidate) is the state. 4 moments.  
**Avoid:** Do not colour the dead leader red; it is gone, not refused. Keep it to four moments.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/leader-election.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)

### websocket-room

**Shows:** Each user holds one open connection to a shared room, and one user's message is fanned out to the others.  
**Picture:** Three user cards in a top row, one room card in a dashed box below, elbow wires with sockets from each user; a counter line in the room card. (7 moments)  
**Fits:** a chat room, a pub/sub topic, a multiplayer session, a shared document  
**Not for:** For one-shot requests; the sockets claim the connections stay open.  
**Borrow:** A counter in the card ('users = 0' to 'users = 3') grows as each connection joins; the broadcast goes out in violet straight lines to the other users only ('sent to 2'). 7 moments.  
**Avoid:** Looks like workers' row-plus-hub but means held connections; do not drop the sockets. Do not send the message back to the sender.  
**Sheet:** `catalogue/websocket-room.png` · **Source:** picture only (drawn by hand; rebuild what you borrow with mk.ts)
